title: Melania Trump grants access to CNN reporter despite her husband's ban
text:
By JON MICHAEL RAASCH, WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT

Published:  03:36 AEST, 22 September 2026   |  Updated:  07:23 AEST, 22 September 2026

234

View  comments

First Lady Melania Trump has offered CNN an olive branch amid its ongoing war with her husband.

President Donald Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House last Friday over allegations of 'fake news.'

The gambit resulted in Secret Service agents seizing press passes from journalists and outlets throwing out coverage plans for the president's trip to the UN General Assembly this week.

CNN, which was previously assigned to send a camera crew and reporter to the UN event, was removed from the White House's traveling press cadre on Sunday.

But the First Lady's Office approved CNN's request to cover Melania this week in Manhattan, according to the outlet's senior White House reporter Betsy Klein.

'Interestingly, we do have one new data point, which is that my credential to cover an event with the First Lady, on the sidelines of the United Nations tomorrow, has been approved,' Klein said on Monday.

CNN was credentialed to cover an announcement the First Lady is expected to give Tuesday at the St. Regis hotel, a source familiar with the matter told the Daily Mail.

The announcement has to do with her 'Fostering the Future Together' initiative, which Melania is expected to touch on repeatedly during her trip to New York for the UN.

Melania Trump's team approved credentials for CNN to cover an event with the First Lady on Tuesday despite the White House ban on the outlet

CNN senior White House reporter Betsy Klein said that she was approved for an event with the First Lady on the sidelines of the UN. She was escorted out of the White House on Saturday after Trump's ban on CNN went into effect

'I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico,' Trump wrote on Friday, announcing the ban

The First Lady's overture toward CNN stands in stark contrast to her husband's treatment of the network.

'I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico,' Trump wrote on Friday, announcing the ban.

'Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report fiction and lies when they’re covering the President of the United States,' he continued.

The following day, reporters from the banned outlets were turned away from the White House when they arrived for work.

Some even had their press passes confiscated by Secret Service agents.

On Monday, Trump doubled down on his ban and tried to explain away how his decision was not 'an assault on the free press.'

Instead, Trump wrote that he is 'instituting an assault on the fake news, some that has grown like cancer in our beloved United States of America.'

In response to the ban, the five major US broadcast networks: Fox News, CNN, CBS, NBC and ABC – together called the TV pool – said in a statement that it would not send a camera crew to cover Trump at the UN after the White House booted CNN from the trip.

White House broadcast tents are seen empty on Monday after Trump's ban

The three media outlets Trump targeted, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, announced they would combat the administration in court over the ban.

'This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes,' they said in a statement released on Monday.

'Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting,' the statement continued.

'Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference.'

US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who Trump appointed in his first term, is presiding over the case and is on familiar legal ground.

In 2018, he ordered the White House to restore CNN journalist Jim Acosta's credentials after his press pass was pulled following a heated clash with Trump.
